name: The Ixchel Priestesses of Cozumel
summary: Sacred female circles dedicated to the Maya goddess of medicine, midwifery, weaving, and the moon.
lore: Long before Spanish contact, women traveled from across Mesoamerica to the coastal island of Cozumel (Isla Mujeres or 'Island of Women'). The priestess circles maintained secret knowledge of botanical medicine, venom-neutralizing remedies, and lunar rituals. Following the Spanish conquest, these indigenous ritual networks went underground, blending ancient Maya healing with European folk practices to form early syncretic brujería traditions.

events.title: The Lunar Eclipse
events.narrative: The moon is swallowed by shadow. The priestesses gather at the island shrine, chanting to return Ixchel's light. The faithful wait in darkness for your word.

choiceA.label: Lead the lunar rite to restore the moon

events.title: The Tizimin Bone-Readers' Challenge
events.narrative: The diviners of Tizimin claim their cracked tortoise shells foretell the downfall of your priestess circle. They demand you acknowledge their supremacy in prophecy.

choiceA.label: Out-read them with the lunar scrying

choiceB.label: Ignore the challenge and grow quietly

events.title: The Valladolid Cenote-Guardians
events.narrative: The keepers of the sacred sinkhole at Valladolid say the spirits in the deep water are angry and have stopped blessing the harvest. They ask your circle to intercede.

choiceA.label: Descend into the cenote and parley

choiceB.label: Bless the harvest from the surface

events.title: The Mérida Moon-Weavers
events.narrative: The city priestesses of Mérida have been weaving lunar energy into cloth and selling blessings in the colonial market, drawing pilgrims away from your island shrine.

choiceA.label: Weave a greater blessing and reclaim the pilgrims

choiceB.label: Undercut their trade in the market

events.title: The Spanish Friar's Sermon
events.narrative: A Spanish friar stands in the colonial square of Mérida, denouncing 'the old goddess-worship of the island' and calling for the shrine to be torn down.

choiceA.label: Debate him before the crowd
choiceA.description: +150 Faith if you win, −6 Followers if you lose

random.winMessage: You match him scripture for scripture and the crowd turns to listen. The friar retreats. +150 Faith.
random.lossMessage: His eloquence sways the crowd. Six of your followers slip away in shame. −6 Followers.

events.title: The Venom-Cure Rite
events.narrative: A child has been bitten by a fer-de-lance in the jungle. The colonial doctor says nothing can be done. The mother runs to your priestesses, begging for the old venom-neutralizing remedy.

choiceA.label: Perform the cure and save the child
choiceA.description: +200 Faith if saved, −6 Followers if lost

random.winMessage: The child's fever breaks by dawn. Word of the old cure spreads across the peninsula. +200 Faith.
random.lossMessage: The child dies despite the rite. The mother's grief turns the village against you. −6 Followers.

choiceB.label: Teach the mother the remedy and let her try

events.title: The Pilgrimage Season
events.narrative: The season of pilgrimage to Isla Mujeres begins. Canoes gather from across the coast, carrying women seeking Ixchel's blessing. The shrine must be ready.

choiceA.label: Prepare the shrine and bless the pilgrims

events.title: The Syncretic Question
events.narrative: A debate divides the circle: blend the old Maya rites with Catholic saints to survive the colonial gaze, or keep the old ways pure and risk destruction.

choiceA.label: Blend the rites with the saints

events.title: A Colonial Noblewoman's Patronage
events.narrative: A Spanish noblewoman arrives at the island shrine with a chest of silver. 'I cannot bear a child. The Church offers only prayer. I am told your goddess knows women's mysteries.'

choiceA.label: Accept her silver and perform the fertility rite

events.title: A Wandering Midwife
events.narrative: A weathered woman with a bundle of Maya herbs arrives at the shrine. 'I have walked from the highlands. I know every birth-song and cord-knot. I seek a circle that honors the old mothers.'
